vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files containing sensitive content (PR/issue bodies) are created in /tmp directory. While random bytes are used for naming, there's a time window between file creation (line 41) and deletion (line 63) where the file could be read by other processes. On Unix systems, /tmp files are typically world-readable by default.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential exposure of PR/issue body content if another process reads the temp file during the operation window

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary file is created with default umask permissions, which may be world-readable. The file should be created with restrictive permissions (0600) to prevent other users from reading sensitive content.
vulnerabilities.impact: Other users on the system could potentially read temporary files containing PR/issue body content

vulnerabilities.description: Memory key validation only checks alphanumeric and underscores. While this prevents directory traversal, the regex pattern doesn't prevent keys like '__proto__' or 'constructor' which could potentially affect object prototype in edge cases.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential prototype pollution if memory operations manipulate object properties unsafely
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

vulnerabilities.description: Session key validation uses the same pattern as memory.js. Restricted key format prevents directory traversal but doesn't prevent prototype pollution attacks.
vulnerabilities.impact: Potential prototype pollution if session context is manipulated through specially crafted keys
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

recommendations.title: Fix Temporary File Permissions in github-safe.js
recommendations.description: Set restrictive file permissions (0600) when creating temporary files to prevent other users from reading sensitive content.
recommendations.implementation: Use fs.writeFileSync with { mode: 0o600 } option when creating temp files on line 41. Alternatively, use os.tmpdir() with proper permissions or use a dedicated secure temp file library.

recommendations.title: Minimize Temporary File Exposure Window
recommendations.description: Consider using piped stdin/stdout instead of temporary files where possible to avoid disk-based exposure of sensitive content.
recommendations.implementation: For github-safe.js, evaluate if using stdin piping with gh command is feasible instead of writing to disk.

recommendations.title: Enhance Key Validation for Prototype Pollution Protection
recommendations.description: Expand validation in memory.js and session.js to explicitly reject dangerous keys like '__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'.
recommendations.implementation: Add blacklist check: if (['__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype'].includes(key)) { throw new Error(...) }

recommendations.title: Regular Dependency Security Audits
recommendations.description: Run npm audit regularly to check for vulnerable dependencies.
recommendations.implementation: Add to CI/CD: npm audit --audit-level=moderate. Update dependencies: npm audit fix

recommendations.title: Review Error Handling in Spawn Operations
recommendations.description: Ensure all spawnSync operations properly handle error states and exit codes.
recommendations.implementation: Add error code checking after spawnSync calls in github-safe.js

recommendations.title: Document Security Assumptions
recommendations.description: Document that helper scripts should only be run in trusted environments (development/CI) and not exposed to untrusted input.
recommendations.implementation: Add security notes to .claude/helpers/README.md or main SECURITY.md

summary.overallAssessment: The codebase demonstrates good security practices with no critical vulnerabilities. The main concern is temporary file handling in the github-safe.js helper script. The application code properly avoids common vulnerabilities (XSS, SQL injection, command injection). Recommendations focus on hardening temp file handling and enhancing input validation.
